title: Jump game — reachable → fewest jumps → prime-3 scoring
label: ag-multi
statement: `nums[i]` is the maximum jump length from index `i`. Starting at index 0, return whether you can reach the **last index**.
provenance: "Dynamic programming — similar to Jump Game" in a Staff Backend Bangkok round (Oct 2025, codingkaro) and "Jump Game with Prime-3 Steps" in an OA (Jun 2025, FastPrep). Stages 1–2 are LeetCode 55 and 45. **Stage 3 is a reconstruction** of the prime-3 variant from its title: moves of 1 or of a prime ending in 3, maximising the score.

stages.title: Can you reach the end?
stages.say: Each value is the maximum jump from that index. Can you reach the last index?

stages.title: Fewest jumps
stages.say: Now return the fewest jumps to reach the end, or −1 if you cannot.

stages.title: Prime-3 scoring
stages.say: A game: from cell i you may move 1 forward, or p forward where p is a prime ending in 3. You must land exactly on the last cell. Maximise the sum of the cells you land on.
testNames: 7 is prime but does not end in 3

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: `nums[i]` is the maximum jump length from index `i`. Starting at index 0, return whether you can reach the **last index**.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can values be 0? (Yes — those are the traps.)
- Is the last index reachable with an exact landing, or is overshooting fine? (Overshooting is fine for stages 1–2.)
- For the scoring variant: must you land exactly on the last cell? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: You never need to know which jump you took, only how far you could get. Sweep left to right keeping the furthest reachable index; the first index beyond it is the dead end. Fewest jumps is the same sweep, counted in layers.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "T."rack the furthest reachable index greedily for reachability and in BFS layers for the fewest jumps, both O(n); the scoring variant is a DP over the allowed step sizes, precomputed with a sieve."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Recursion or DP over all jumps — O(n²) or worse.
- Missing the 0 that traps you.
- Treating 1 as prime, or forgetting the step of 1, in the scoring variant.
- int overflow on i + nums[i].
